title: Reduced 16-Layer Quarter-Wave Stack Initialized at 10.5 μm
scientific_hypothesis: A reduced 16-layer HfO2/SiO2 stack with quarter-wave optical thickness initialization centered at 10.5 μm (midpoint of 8-13 μm emission band) will produce physically valid candidates where 24-layer stacks failed, while maintaining sufficient spectral selectivity through constructive interference in the target band.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack design principle: alternating high/low index layers with optical thickness λ/4 at target wavelength creates high reflectance (low emissivity) outside the target band through Bragg reflection, while allowing transmission (high emissivity via Kirchhoff's law) within the design band.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Si substrate (16 finite layers, 8 pairs)
soft_objectives: maintain physical validity of all candidates
manufacturing_considerations: 16 layers reduces fabrication complexity vs 24 layers
thickness bounds 200-1800 nm avoid boundary singularities that caused material_data failures
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for spectral filtering
Kirchhoff's law relating absorptance to emissivity for thermal emitters
expected_advantages: Lower layer count reduces optimization complexity and material_data failure risk
Initialization at 10.5 μm centers the high-emissivity band
Thickness bounds away from 2000 nm limit avoid boundary-related solver failures
known_risks: 16 layers may provide insufficient spectral selectivity compared to 24 layers
Quarter-wave initialization may not capture optimal aperiodic solution
execution_request_english: Optimize a 16-layer planar dielectric stack on Si substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (16 finite layers). Initialize thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness for 10500 nm wavelength using HfO2 and SiO2 refractive indices in the 8-13 μm range. Allow all 16 thicknesses to vary during optimization with bounds 200-1800 nm. Evaluate spectral absorptance from 3000-13000 nm. Target: maximize absorptance in 8000-13000 nm, minimize absorptance in 3000-5000 nm. Include deterministic fallback: if stochastic optimizer yields valid_candidates=0, inject three periodic quarter-wave templates with 8, 10, and 12 layer pairs at 10500 nm center wavelength. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3000-5000 nm, 8000-13000 nm. soft objectives: high emissivity in 8000-13000 nm; low emissivity in 3000-5000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high emissivity in 3000-5000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 24.
revision_reason: Reduced layer count from 24 to 16 to address material_data failure in iteration_06; shifted thickness bounds from 2000 nm maximum to 1800 nm to avoid boundary singularities; added deterministic periodic template fallback per feedback directives.
